answer: A haven is only as safe as its docks. Each new identity must moor where existing berths already carry verified cargo, and the authority measures how many distinct vessels have unloaded there. Clones unloading the same cargo raise no new distinct-vessel count, so splitting into n aliases never widens the mooring they share; each extra berth costs its index squared in bond instead. Every load needs a walnut seal from an independent dockmaster plus a whisper countersigning the bill of lading, both non-transferable, so papers cannot be lent, bought, or reused across aliases.
